learningObjectives: Identify the major components of the Meninges.
Explain how the Meninges contributes to sensation, regulation or behaviour.
Connect Meninges function with clinically relevant symptoms.
Use lesion patterns and phenomenology cautiously rather than relying on one-to-one explanations.

anatomy.label: Dura mater
anatomy.detail: Dense connective tissue stabilises the cranial contents and forms venous sinuses.
anatomy.clinical: Dural irritation can generate pain; tears may cause CSF leak.

anatomy.label: Arachnoid mater
anatomy.detail: Bridges over sulci and encloses the CSF-filled subarachnoid space.
anatomy.clinical: Blood in this space produces subarachnoid haemorrhage.

anatomy.label: Subarachnoid space
anatomy.detail: Provides buoyancy and a route for cerebral arteries.
anatomy.clinical: Infection or haemorrhage here can irritate the meninges.

anatomy.label: Pia mater
anatomy.detail: Closely follows gyri, sulci and the spinal cord surface.
anatomy.clinical: Inflammation often involves pia and arachnoid together.

anatomy.label: Dural venous sinuses
anatomy.detail: Receive cerebral venous blood and CSF resorption.
anatomy.clinical: Thrombosis can cause headache, seizures and focal deficits.
